name: RTX 3070 tech tree
scope: Get the most real work from one RTX 3070 8 GB (LHR included) for local LLMs and agent work.

status_values.measured: Done. result holds measured values with source paths.
status_values.paused: Started, then stopped. Not measured, so dependents wait. It restarts from scratch on the next run.
status_values.queued: Ready, or ready once its prereqs are measured.
status_values.needs_owner: Needs the owner present or the owner's go. The runner skips it.
status_values.blocked: A prereq is needs_owner or blocked. The runner skips it.

rules: Run a node only when every prereq has status measured.
Pick the first runnable node in next_order.
Each result entry has metric, value, source (a path relative to the repo root) and an optional note.
Label every number with n, warm or cold, and its confounds. Never invent a number.

limits: Do not change the power limit, clocks or undervolt.
Do not reboot, shut down or sleep the machine while unlocked.
Do not write firmware, VBIOS, ESP, BCD or NVRAM.
VBIOS flashing is out of scope, permanently. The firmware track is driver, CUDA and firmware version research and inventory only.
A WSL2 memory-cap change needs the owner's go.
Cold-boot arms need the owner present.
Stop if the screen blanks under load and log power and temperature.

out_of_scope.why: Owner decision. Firmware work stays at driver, CUDA and version research and inventory. Not a node, not blocked: excluded.

measurement_rules: State n for every number. llama-bench uses -r 5 and 3 reps where possible.
Label warm or cold. All results in v1.3.0 are warm.
Keep the display on the integrated GPU for A/B runs, or label the confound.
Report pass rates with 95% confidence intervals.
A target is a goal, not a result.

baseline.label: unlocked agent bench, partial offload, warm
baseline.inferred_note: The -ngl, ctx and KV values are the lab defaults at that time. They are inferred from the serve script defaults, not from a log of the launch line.

config_tiers.rule: Each tier stacks on the tier below. A tier counts only after it meets the pass criteria against the tier below on the frozen held-out set. Config files are published for C0 and C1. For C2 and up, the result and how it was measured are published.

pass_criteria.set: Frozen held-out set (heldout-set node): at least 72 tasks, 6 roles x 12, never used for tuning. Same task order, harness and power logging for both tiers. One run per task per tier at minimum (n >= 72 paired runs).
pass_criteria.anchors: c0-anchor and c1-anchor must complete every held-out run before any higher tier is compared.
pass_criteria.beat: A tier beats the tier below if at least one holds: (a) pass rate: paired on the same tasks, exact McNemar one-sided p < 0.05 for more passes (equivalently the 95% CI of the paired pass-rate difference is above 0); (b) passes per hour at least 1.10x; (c) median agent decode tok/s at least 1.10x.
pass_criteria.no_regression: And none of these regress beyond the margin: pass rate, the lower bound of the 95% CI of the paired difference above -5 percentage points (non-inferiority); passes per hour at least 0.95x; median agent decode tok/s at least 0.95x; board Wh per pass at most 1.10x.
pass_criteria.fit: Fits in 8 GB: peak VRAM logged at 1 s for the whole run, at most 8192 MiB, zero out-of-memory errors. For C6 and up also log peak system RAM and swap; peak RAM must stay below the WSL2 cap minus 2 GiB.
pass_criteria.report: Report n, both tiers' pass rates with 95% Wilson CIs, the paired table (both pass, only upper, only lower, neither), passes per hour, decode tok/s, Wh per pass and peak VRAM MiB.

tiers.goal: Know the stack, measure it the same way every time, and confirm the FP32-accumulate unlock.

tiers.title: Config tiers
tiers.goal: Stack the wins into numbered configs C0 to C7. Each tier must beat the tier below on a frozen held-out task set.

tiers.title: Inference
tiers.goal: Get the most tokens per second from 8 GB of VRAM.

tiers.title: Agent reliability
tiers.goal: Make more agent tasks pass on the same model and card.

tiers.title: Throughput
tiers.goal: Keep the card busy while agents wait on builds and tests.

tiers.goal: Measure energy per passing task. Do not tune power.

tiers.goal: Keep the server up around the clock within stock limits: pause, restart, thermals, uptime.

tiers.goal: Combine the wins into a bigger model class and more useful work per Wh.

Label: fit-map speeds (pp512, tg128) are measured at llama-bench's short context (512-token prompt, 128 generated tokens), not at the largest context that fits. Speed at the max context is lower.

Label: the on-disk lab Qwen3-8B Q4_K_M has the repo file's size (5027783488 bytes) but not its sha256 (on-disk begins 9180c8dd, Qwen/Qwen3-8B-GGUF begins d98cdcbd). nodes.title: Sampler settings
nodes.goal: Test recommended sampler settings against the lab defaults.
nodes.test: Two sampler arms, sent per request with no server change. 36-run core agent bench on the best config. Each arm is compared with the same base run.
nodes.metric: Passes per hour (decision), pass rate, loop events per run, tool-call errors, Wh per task, truncations per role.
nodes.target: Keep an arm only if its passes per hour beat the base config. If both do, keep the higher one. Loop events and pass rate are reported, not used to decide.
confounds: The arms run one after the other, not interleaved. Each is compared with the same base run.

nodes.title: Planner-only thinking
nodes.goal: Test whether bounded thinking helps the planner role.

nodes.metric: Passes per hour, pass rate (overall and pm), board Wh per task, truncated tool calls and length stops per role (baseline 9 of 363 calls in the full-offload run: write 5, edit 4).
nodes.target: Keep only if passes per hour beat the base config. Report the pm pass rate and pm truncations separately.

result.metric: baseline output-limit truncations, full-offload run (not this node's result)
result.value: 9 of 363 tool calls (write 5, edit 4). The earlier count of 14 included 5 bash errors by a keyword match.

confounds: Thinking tokens share the role output cap. Truncations are logged per role.

nodes.target: Target: aggregate tok/s per board W at least 1.5x of 1 slot, at the largest slot count that fits.
confounds: Half-full batches can be the worst case (public reports).
8192 per slot covers the agent-task context p95 of about 6.2k tokens (6248, n=60, results/full-offload.md).

nodes.title: Pause handoff with no lost state
nodes.goal: Give the GPU to another app (for example a game) and take it back with no lost model state.
nodes.test: Install the prepared 24/7 package: slot save on pause, slot restore on start. Use the full-offload config. Put a long context in slot 0 with a known fact in the middle. Run 20 pause and start cycles through the package commands. After each restore, ask for the fact. This tests the pause and start path only: the game watcher logs games but does not pause the server (auto-pause-trigger).
nodes.metric: Pause wall s, resume wall s, slot save and restore ms, slot file MB, restores that answer the fact correctly, time to first token after restore vs cold re-read, VRAM after stop.
nodes.target: Target: 20 of 20 restores answer the fact correctly. Pause and resume each under 10 s wall. VRAM after stop under 1.5 GB.
confounds: An earlier pause bench at -ngl 30, ctx 65536, KV q4_0/q4_0 measured pause under 7 s wall and slot restore in 180 to 391 ms (source: results/pause-bench.md). The full-offload config uses KV q8_0/q8_0, so slot files are larger. Measure again at this config.
The package defaults (ctx 24576, -ngl 30) are not the full-offload config. Set the full-offload values before the test.
Lab finding: the game watcher only logs a game start. It does not call the pause. The automatic trigger is a separate node, auto-pause-trigger.
safety_notes: Stop on any screen blanking. No power, clock or undervolt changes.
The watcher never stops or touches the other app. It only pauses and resumes the model server.

nodes.title: Watchdog and auto-restart
nodes.goal: Bring the server back by itself after a crash, with state restored.
nodes.test: Run the server under the package supervisor (restart on failure, back-off from 10 s to 5 min). Kill the server process 10 times: idle, mid-request and mid-save. Measure time to healthy and the restore result after each kill.
nodes.metric: Time to healthy s (median, max), restarts that restored state, requests lost per kill, supervisor give-ups, corrupt slot files.
nodes.target: Target: 10 of 10 kills back healthy in under 30 s. No restart loop. Zero corrupt slot files.
confounds: The supervisor gives up after 8 failures in 15 min by design. A give-up is a result, not a fault of the test.
A kill mid-save can leave a partial slot file. Count it, and check that restore falls back to a cold start.

Expected finding: the systemd back-off (10 s growing to 5 min over 6 steps) will probably miss the 30 s target from kill 3 on. Record time to healthy and the back-off step for each kill; a miss caused by the back-off is a result, not a test fault.
safety_notes: Kill only the model server process. No reboot, shutdown or sleep.

nodes.title: Thermals soak within stock limits
nodes.goal: Show the card holds its speed under hours of load at stock limits.
nodes.test: Run the C1 config with the agent task mix for 4 h, requests sent straight to the server with no request proxy. Read temperature, board W, clocks and throttle reasons every 5 s. Logging only.
nodes.metric: Max and p95 GPU temperature C, share of samples with each throttle reason, decode tok/s in the first hour vs the last hour, mean board W.
nodes.target: Target: last-hour decode tok/s within 5% of the first hour. No thermal throttle reason. No screen blanking.
confounds: Room temperature changes the result. Log it if a sensor is there, or label it as not logged.

Full offload runs near the 220 W power limit (203.1 W mean, results/full-offload.md). A software power-cap throttle reason is the stock limit at work, not a thermal fault. Report it apart from thermal reasons.
safety_notes: Read-only logging. No power-limit, clock, fan or undervolt changes.
Stop on any screen blanking.

nodes.title: Long soak test
nodes.goal: Find faults that show only after a full day of load.
nodes.test: Run the C1 config for 24 h with a mixed request load sent straight to the server, no request proxy: short chat, 2000-token and 6000-token prompts, agent tasks. Pause and resume at random times. Log errors, restarts, VRAM and system RAM every minute.
nodes.metric: Errors per 1000 requests, restarts, decode tok/s drift per hour, VRAM and system RAM growth per hour, slot disk use.
nodes.target: Target: under 1 error per 1000 requests. VRAM and RAM growth under 1% per hour. Each unplanned restart recovered by the watchdog.
confounds: The request mix sets the result. Publish the mix with the result.
Runs last, so it does not hold up any tier.
safety_notes: Same limits as thermal-soak. Stop on any screen blanking.

nodes.title: Uptime and SLO metrics
nodes.goal: Observe how much of each day the server is up and inside its latency targets. Background observer: it blocks no node.
nodes.test: Start the 24/7 package metrics (one sample per minute, daily rollups) after pause-handoff and leave them on for at least 7 days while other nodes run. Compute uptime outside pauses, pause minutes, restore results and request latency. The chain does not wait for it.
nodes.metric: Server up share outside pauses, paused minutes per day, restores ok and failed, health timeouts, p50 and p95 time to first token, decode tok/s per request.
nodes.target: Target: up share outside pauses at least 99%. All restores ok. p95 time to first token under 5 s at 2000-token prompts.
confounds: WSL nvidia-smi utilization counts the whole GPU, Windows apps too. Count GPU busy only over unpaused minutes (source: the 24/7 package notes).
safety_notes: Logging only.
